title: rujinlong/nf-phamseek pipeline parameters
description: Phage detection in low-biomass clinical Oxford Nanopore metagenomes.

input.help_text: CSV with a header row. `sample_id` must be unique and free of whitespace. `fastq` may be absolute or relative to the samplesheet's own directory. `platform` defaults to `ont` (the only one implemented). `sample_type` is one of `sample`, `ntc`, `positive_control`; taxa also seen in an `ntc` are flagged in the report, but never subtracted.

mode.description: Analysis tier, or `setup` to download the reference databases. Only `fast` is implemented.
mode.help_text: `fast` is read-level: QC, kraken2, two-level host depletion, bracken, report. `full` would add assembly (flye), geNomad and CheckV; it is deliberately not wired up and fails immediately with an explanation rather than running a partial path.

database_options.title: Reference databases
database_options.description: Databases are always external to the repository and are never copied into the work directory.

host_index.description: Directory holding the host reference (.mmi or FASTA). Overrides <db_dir>/host.

db_has_decoy.description: Whether the kraken2 database contains non-phage decoy sequences: auto (default), true or false.
db_has_decoy.help_text: `auto` (default) reads the database's own taxonomy with kraken2-inspect and reports the human, bacterial and plasmid decoy classes separately, so an unverifiable class is marked unknown rather than guessed. `true`/`false` override that with an operator declaration; when a declaration contradicts what the database actually contains, the report says so instead of reasoning from the wrong premise. This matters because it selects the false-positive caveat: without plasmid decoy sequences roughly 37% of plasmid-derived sequence is called phage, with them at or below 0.4%. Raising --kraken2_confidence does not fix that, because the signal is real homology (shared integrase and relaxase modules), not stray k-mers.

db_label.description: Human-readable database name recorded in the report and manifest.

db_component.description: With --mode setup, which database component to download.

chopper_min_quality.description: Minimum mean Phred quality per read (chopper -q).

host_depletion_options.title: Host depletion
host_depletion_options.description: Two levels. Level 1 deletes the host subtree using the kraken2 pass that has already been paid for; level 2 aligns the remainder against the host reference. A kraken2 decoy only relabels reads, so level 2 is what makes the deletion complete.

skip_host_removal.description: Skip the level-2 aligner. Level 1 still runs.
skip_host_removal.help_text: Leaves any host read the database does not recognise in the output. Intended for development and for databases with well-characterised host decoy content, not for data that leaves the institution.

host_taxid.description: Root of the host subtree to delete at level 1.

viral_taxid.description: Root of the viral subtree counted as evidence.

l2_input.description: Which reads the level-2 aligner sees.
l2_input.help_text: `all_nonhuman` (default) sends every read outside the host subtree to the aligner, so a human read misclassified as viral is still caught. `nonhuman_nonviral` withholds viral-classified reads: marginally faster, but it opens exactly that gap.

minimap2_preset.help_text: Must match the preset the .mmi index was built with; minimap2 silently honours the index's parameters over the command line.

kraken2_confidence.help_text: 0.02, not kraken2's default of 0. Against a phage reference database the default calls a taxon on a single k-mer hit, which made 61% of human and 38% of clean bacterial contigs look like phage in the benchmark this pipeline derives from. Do NOT raise it: short-read intuition does not transfer to ONT. Going from 0.02 to 0.10 costs only ~3.5 points of recall on 150 bp reads at 0.1% error, but 15 points at 95% read identity (typical R10.4 simplex) and 29 points at 87% identity, because each ONT read carries far fewer exactly-matching k-mers to vote with. Raising it also does not remove plasmid and ICE false positives, which come from real shared modules rather than stray k-mers.

run_bracken.description: Run bracken abundance re-estimation (off by default).
run_bracken.help_text: Off by default on purpose: bracken re-estimates abundance from a k-mer distribution built for one fixed read length, an assumption ONT reads violate by construction. Kraken2 read counts and the RPM derived from them are reported regardless and do not depend on bracken. If you enable it, set bracken_read_length from the median read length of your own run -- there is no defensible default. Bracken is also skipped automatically, with a warning, when the database has no database<N>mers.kmer_distrib files.

bracken_read_length.description: Read length whose k-mer distribution bracken should use. Required with --run_bracken; no default, because ONT runs differ.

bracken_threshold.description: Minimum reads for bracken to re-estimate a taxon.

reporting_options.title: Reporting thresholds
reporting_options.description: phamseek reports read-level evidence only, so every positive is a candidate. These thresholds decide how a candidate is graded, not whether it is confirmed.

min_reads.description: Minimum reads for a taxon to be graded above `below_threshold`.

min_rpm.description: Minimum reads per million non-host reads for `candidate_passes_abundance_screen`.
min_rpm.help_text: The denominator is non-host reads, not total reads: in plasma and CSF the human fraction dominates, and normalising by total reads would make the same organism look far rarer in a sample that simply had more host background.

skip_krona.help_text: One interactive chart per sample plus one for the whole run, written to <sample>/krona/ and summary/phamseek_krona.html. The charts cover the NON-HOST subtree: in plasma and CSF the host dominates the report, and charting it as well compresses everything else into an unreadable sliver. This also puts the chart on the same denominator as --min_rpm, which is already per million non-host reads. The pages are self-contained -- Krona inlines its JavaScript -- so they open with no network access.

max_cpus.description: Maximum CPUs any single task may request.

max_memory.description: Maximum memory any single task may request.
max_memory.help_text: kraken2 loads the whole database into RAM, so this must exceed the database size. The 11 GB production database peaks around 12 GB.

max_time.description: Maximum time any single task may request.

help.description: Print the parameter list, or the full entry for one named parameter.
help.help_text: `--help` prints every non-hidden parameter. `--help <parameter>` prints the long description of that one parameter. Add `--show_hidden` to include parameters marked hidden. The help text is rendered by the pipeline from nextflow_schema.json rather than by the schema plugin, so it works under both Nextflow syntax parsers.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use colour in the log output.

validate_params.description: Validate parameters against this schema at startup.
